target_customer: Startups and SMBs in Mexico with idle cash
problem: SMB treasuries sat idle in low yield bank accounts with no accessible investment or cash management tools.
business_model: Regulated treasury platform, fees on assets or advice

founders.name: Salvador Rivero
technical: Sciences Po, Political Science and Finance
previous_startups: Described himself as a third-time founder (names not given)

exit.reason: Not public; Dealroom says it ceased operations while registering as an independent investment advisor with the CNBV

technical_complexity.rationale: Required regulated investment flows and custodian integration (Kuspit) in Mexico, hard for a six person team.

defensibility.rationale: A CNBV registration could protect but was still in process; product was otherwise copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not documented; the company ceased operations.

market_need_then: Mexican fintechs were competing on yield for idle balances in 2021 to 2022; SMB treasury demand not quantified in sources.

brand_strength.rationale: No brand coverage found beyond a podcast interview with the founder.

outcome_analysis: Levo started operating in Mexico around August 2022 with about 200 clients and a goal of managing the savings of 100,000 people within three years. It was still registering as an investment advisor with the CNBV when it ceased operations, and only a tiny seed was found. The exact cause is not public, so the failure factors are tentative: regulatory delay and no visible later round.
